newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - Polish repo/revrepo seen down by end '97.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Polish repo/revrepo seen down by end '97.

text.p: Banks expect the central bank's repo and reverse repo rates to ease by year-end with more players predicting reverse repos than repos, a Reuters poll of Poland's 26 biggest banks showed.

Banks predicted the National Bank of Poland's 14-day revrepo rate, last at 22.15 percent, would fall to 19.09 percent by year-end. The forecast is a mean average of banks' predictions ranging from 16.50 to 22.00 percent.
Last month banks saw the revrepo rate down to 18.89 percent.

Banks expected the reverse repo rate to stabilise this month at 22.11 percent with a range from 21.50 to 22.35 percent and to fall to 18.05 percent in April 1998 with a range from 14.80 to 21.90 percent.
Seven of the polled banks expected the central bank would stage both reverse repo and repo operations or only repos at the end of the year.

The repo rate at the end of 1997 was seen at 20.06 percent on average with a range of predictions from 17.60 to 23.75 percent. The repo rate was seen at 22.46 percent on average in April and at 19.33 percent in April 1998.
